state.objective: Can must remove copied upstream SQLite grammar/runtime from its tracked source tree and use pinned normal external Go modules in the shared cache. Replacing copied C with copied Go, archives, submodules or another vendor tree is forbidden. Native Bun.SQL execution and the intended checked-raw-SQL contract stay. No external consumers need compatibility. Codex decides and reviews; Muse executes the complete saved checklist. No benchmarks or broad builds are authorized on the 256GB laptop.
state.contract: The compiler owns Analysis: statement count/kind and source byte spans, every bind occurrence/index in source order, top-level SELECT LIMIT shape, RETURNING and positioned syntax failures. Descriptor checks enforce one admitted statement, parameter coverage/name matching, exclusive trailing LIMIT binding, non-returning DML execute and INSERT RETURNING under one. Exact segments drive native tags; runtime validates returned records. Schema proof and limits on all database work are not promised. Parser identity must distinguish a pinned release/content from Tree-sitter ABI alone. PostgreSQL still requires cgo; distribution preserves CGO_ENABLED=1 and GOPROXY=off after prefetch.
state.official: The exact existing grammar resolves as github.com/defin/tree-sitter-sqlite3 v0.1.1-0.20260503135658-7f69bb66845b; parser/scanner/header hashes match local copies. Paired with official github.com/tree-sitter/go-tree-sitter v0.25.0, actual SetLanguage and parsing succeed at ABI15. The runtime proxy pin resolves with verified sums at adc13ffd8b2c0b01b878fda9f7c422ce0df5fad3 although its live GitHub tag is absent. Archive sources are complete. An adapter matched the current backend across 74 cases. It needs exact-once parser/tree/cursor Close, missing-node handling, explicit rejection of ordinary malformed-literal nodes, and bounded iterative traversal. Plain Parse avoids a suspected options-pointer lifetime gap. C and cgo remain only in external modules.
state.meyer: github.com/sqlc-dev/meyer v0.1.2 resolves normally with verified sums at commit 59b2dbf9b1872316bc6c6d3379b500df84db3e01. It is independently authored Go, MIT, Go1.24 and has zero module dependencies. sqlc main imports it, but the inspected sqlc release does not; maintenance history is short. The 74-case probe returns the needed AST/spans, including UTF-8, CTEs, nested limits, DML and binds inside RETURNING. Differences include full-sigil name identities, digit/Tcl names, optional mutation LIMIT, diagnostic wording/positions and semicolon-inclusive statement spans. LIMIT-comma AST children reorder operands, so sites must be sorted by byte position. Its existing BindParam.Number already implements SQLite numbering and should be reused.
state.guards_and_limits: Meyer has a fixed parser recursion guard of 10000: bounded probes parsed a 40035-byte expression chain and 5000 nested parentheses, while 15000 nesting failed cleanly. A 100000-term chain also parsed; these were correctness checks, not timing/footprint measurements. Parse(ctx,Reader) ignores context and reads without limit; choose ParseString behind a 1MiB input ceiling. Lexer NUL stops parsing, so reject NUL before the call. ast.Walk is separately recursive and unsafe for arbitrarily deep flat-expression trees; use iterative Node.Children traversal capped at one million nodes and sort/validate bind spans. No hard heap/time bound is claimed. Tree-sitter also passed bounded chains/nesting but native allocation failure can abort. Full upstream corpora, all target platforms and staged bundles were not reproduced.
state.verified_policy: Independent Bun1.4.2 in-memory SQLite checks bind :a/@a/$a to separate values and accept $1 as a named parameter. Malformed X'01001' and 123abc are rejected. #name prepares in SQLite but lies outside Can's documented placeholder family. The old code/documentation described sigil collapsing and digit-name rejection as engine behavior incorrectly; there is no independently motivated Can compatibility requirement for these mistakes. Keep declared suffix-to-field checking, which can reject digit/Tcl application names even when parsing accepts them; limit names remain unrestricted. Do not rewrite native statement spans merely to mimic old punctuation boundaries. Grammar differences must be reconciled against engine observations and intended admission, not only old goldens.
state.engine_arbitration: Muse's schema-backed in-memory Bun1.4.2/SQLite3.54.0 checks now confirm acceptance of numeric and Tcl names and separate sigils. UPDATE..LIMIT and DELETE..ORDER BY..LIMIT also execute, so Meyer must use Options{UpdateDeleteLimit:true}. Both parsers accept ?0 and overflowing numbered binds, but existing Can CheckSites rejects their zero/invalid indexes; keep that guard. Both accept LIMIT before a later UNION, rejected by the engine: add a narrow structural check for misplaced LIMIT/ORDER BY on nonfinal compound cores rather than recreate preparation. Engine accepts depth2000 and rejects5000 while both parsers accept5000; do not imitate a build-dependent preparation resource ceiling with a new handwritten scanner. Retain the stated compiler input/traversal guards and disclose that parser acceptance does not guarantee engine preparation. No new owned repository is needed on current evidence.

production_parser.instructions: Which production SQLite parser should Can integrate now, given the qualified options and the stated small adapter guards? Choose for this no-vendoring migration without weakening intended checks or claiming unmeasured speed benefits. Your answer is advisory; independently reviewed implementation and tests remain required.

criteria.meyer: Integrate pinned Meyer v0.1.2 with pre-parse byte/NUL guards, iterative bounded traversal, sorted byte spans and its native bind numbering; update release metadata and deliberate policy differences. Remove all local SQLite parser C and the obsolete bridge.
criteria.official: Integrate the verified defin grammar and official v0.25.0 runtime modules, with exact-once native ownership, bounded traversal, failure-node corrections and deliberate parameter/policy updates. Remove repository-owned upstream C but retain external native compilation.
criteria.further_evidence: Neither candidate is sufficiently supported for integration yet; identify this as a need for additional bounded correctness evidence before selecting, without publishing a new parser repository or redesigning SQL.
